thesis: Maze of Ith turned a land slot into repeatable combat control, preventing damage while also untapping the attacker and creating timing decisions that ordinary removal never offered.

competitiveTimeline.significance: Maze moved from early defensive decks into Lands, control, and Commander, where its lack of mana production remains the real cost of its unusually durable interaction.

playbook.role: Hold Maze for the attacker that matters most, and remember that it can target your own creature after combat damage to remove it from combat or create vigilance-like lines under older rules interactions.
